comment: Lol they're raising Premium AGAIN while Discover Weekly is full of AI slop and artists get pennies per stream. I already left once. This is the push I needed. Cancelling and buying straight from Bandcamp, pay the artists.

Glad I cancelled back when the AI songs started flooding my recs. Now they want more money for the same songs on repeat in rotation. Enjoy your loyal customers, Spotify, you're down to the ones who stayed out of inertia.

Ugh, another bump. Does the new price hit people on gift cards or multi-month blocks, or only the monthly billing? Last time my account showed Free after a gift card purchase and support just sent the same copy-paste reply. Anyone know what happens to the billing period ends date?

Student went from 5.99 to 6.99. Annoying, but still the cheapest way to get ad-free music. My real worry is whether the Hulu bundle survives the next re-verification, because that is the only reason I'm on the student plan. Does the new price apply to existing student accounts or only new signups?

A dollar more doesn't bother me much. Nobody gets lossless out of this either, and Bluetooth compresses everything anyway so I'm not missing much. 320 is still fine for me, so I'm not switching over a price bump.

Paying more for a player that still restarts songs and closes the Mix feature halfway through? Nah. Apple Music is going to be the move. Lossless sounds great on good speakers but not for an extra dollar when the basics are broken, lol.

Family goes from 19.99 to 21.99 and we still don't get lossless or the AI playlists where I live. Same price as everyone else, fewer features. I keep paying because it's worth its weight in gold for my parents, but it's frustrating that the price keeps moving while the features stay region locked.

so they raise the price and the bug that's been wrecking my app since october is still here?? same issue here, tried reinstalling everything. if it's still not working by my billing date I'm going to try YouTube Music. hopefully fixed soon but I'm not paying more for this.

Great, more money for an app that keeps removing features and adding ads. Crossfade is still hiding in settings and the Hide button is still gone. Spicetify is the only reason I'm not losing my mind. Still paying because the app is convenient, but this is getting old.

A price increase with still no true lossless? Cheaper services have had hi-res for years. I'm mostly on Tidal for sound now and keep Spotify for recommendations, so this makes the Spotify half a harder sell. Not leaving yet because moving the library is a pain.

Duo going up $2, meh. Shrug. I mostly care about Discover Weekly and it still doesn't refresh half the time for me. If the new price comes with features that actually show up on my account, fine, but I'm not paying more for promised stuff that never arrives.

Yeah, 12.99 now. It's pricey but still cheaper than buying the albums, and I'd pay it. The ads still playing on Premium are my real gripe, but for daily listening it's still worth it for me. Been paying since forever and no complaints here.

Another price bump, great. I already pay for YouTube Premium and it comes with YouTube Music, so Spotify is getting harder to justify with AI music and the same recs on repeat. Jam keeps me here for now, but if the algorithm doesn't get better I'm moving over.

So I'm paying more for Premium and I still get unskippable Spotify ads in my podcasts? Premium is supposed to mean no ads. I already moved my shows to Apple Podcasts and I'm not paying more for double dipping. One more ad and I'm deleting my account.

Spotify raises prices again and artists still get pennies for their streams. The subscription money goes to a royalty pool that labels, stock music and AI tracks keep taking a cut of. I'd rather buy music directly from the artists. I'm done paying into this money vacuum.

Two price bumps now and I still think $12.99 is a steal for nearly everything ever recorded, ad-free and downloadable for flights. Streaming should pay artists and this is how you do it. Still worth it for me.

Premium going up again? Pass. I'm already on free and my playlists still play random songs for me. Apple Music is cheaper and I've moved before, so if playback keeps breaking I'll probably go there again. For now I'm just annoyed.

Family plan going up by $2, annoying, but it's still cheap per person and I'm not moving my podcasts, audiobooks and Connect setup to another app. Still worth every penny for us. Just wish they'd stop raising it every year.

Cool, Premium goes up again and I still can't get the next song to play half the time. Support is useless. Amazon Music is cheaper and has playlists Spotify is missing, so I'm going there. Moving playlists is a pain but so is this.

I'm on free so the Premium bump doesn't touch me, but it's ridiculous that Premium keeps going up for a few extras. Why do I have to pay for skips and song picking? Free is where I'll be, with ads and whatever features they unlock for me this month.

Ugh. Another price hike and the podcast side is still broken: New Episodes folder is gone and episodes play in reverse. I keep Spotify for the playlists and the UI, but if this keeps going I'll move my shows to Pocket Casts. Stupidest update yet.

More money for Premium and the shuffle is still dogshit. I already went back to free once and free shuffles better than my premium did for years. Same 10-15 songs over and over. I'm about to be back on free.

Premium goes up, nope. I'm not paying more when the free tier is nearly unusable. Buy YouTube Premium if you want features, or grab a cheaper country plan like everyone else. Free Spotify is ass but I'm staying on it.

Family to $21.99 means about $3.66 a slot if we split it six ways, which still beats most things, but I'm not thrilled. A $2 bump and there's still no lossless on the plan. I'll probably look at Amazon Music if the next bump lands.

Spotify going up again while Apple Music is already cheaper with better audio. I've been stuck here for the playlists but I'm finally moving to Apple Music for real. Recommendations keep repeating the same songs anyway, so there's not much to keep me here.

Family plan going up while the discography is still hidden and the lyrics screen is ugly? Hell no. The artist button took forever to fix and now this. I'm back to YouTube Music, screw the monthly subscription.

I love Spotify but the price keeps creeping up and Discover Weekly still plays the same top-40 songs. I still need the library for transcribing so I'm not going anywhere, I just wish the recommendations were worth paying for. Love-hate relationship, as always.

The price going up is annoying but I'm not rebuilding 300-plus playlists somewhere else to save a couple of bucks. Search and multi-device sync are still the reason I'm here. If the UI keeps moving the wrong way I'll reconsider.
